Visiting The Ohio State Fair For Less

By
Melanie Bange
-
August 1, 2026
0
Facebook
Twitter
Pinterest
ReddIt
Email
    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 4:31
    Instaread

    The Ohio State Fair is one of our favorite events to attend annually, but the cost can rack up very quickly. While the Fair does have many free things to view, such as the Butter Cow display, food and ride costs alone can make the event feel unattainable. Throughout the years, we have learned where the cleanest bathrooms are and ways to get the best “bang for our buck.”

    Admission purchases can be done by the day or for the entire Fair. With that said, we love to snag an admission deal. More specifically, we love to use our Ohio History Membership for FREE admission. This can be accessed through the Ohio History Connection and includes free parking, admission, and a golf cart shuttle ride directly into the Fairgrounds!

    If you do not have an Ohio History Membership, pre-purchase tickets to save a few dollars. Just a reminder: Kids under 5 years old, as well as active and retired military members, receive FREE daily admission.

    Be sure to pack snacks and a picnic lunch. Per The Ohio State Fair’s policy, purses, backpacks, coolers, and strollers are permitted but are subject to search. The Fair encourages you to bring your own food and non-alcoholic beverages. Metal and plastic containers are permitted.

    There are endless free activities at The Ohio State Fair. We always recommend looking at the daily schedule for times and locations. Our favorite spaces to explore include:

    The Dairy Barn: Hosting cow milking simulations and housing the famous Butter Cow, The Dairy Barn is a must-do. We particularly love looking at the details carved into the butter display!

    Ohio Department of Natural Resources Section: We could spend the whole day just in this area! With outdoor activity simulations (like kayaking and fishing), a playground, Smokey Bear, a butterfly house, and hands-on environmental experiences, this area is entirely free!

    The Petting Zoo: From farm animals to safari animals, you may come face-to-face with a zebra or an emu! Exploring is included with admission; depending on the animals and time of day, feeding opportunities may cost extra.

    We despise purchasing ride wristbands but have found the most relaxing ride to the front gate is the Sky Glider. For $3 per person for a one-way ride, it is a great way to enjoy the views and people-watch!

    By far, the largest expense can be food. If you are a fair food lover and want to buy a few snacks, look into Three Dollar Thursday. During opening day on Thursday, many vendors offer a special item for $3. This may be a smaller funnel cake, half an ear of grilled corn, or a 12-ounce shaken lemonade instead of a meal-sized item; however, your waist and wallet will thank you!

    If you cannot make it to the Ohio State Fair on Thursday, look at the Fair’s website for vendor coupons. In 2026, there are three printable pages of coupons. Personally, we are looking forward to saving a few dollars at Glass City Pizzeria in the new Ohio Showcase Building Food Hall!

    Speaking of new spaces, the Ohio State Fair’s large construction projects are finally complete! New in 2026 are a plethora of exciting additions. Spaces we are thrilled to explore include:

    Ohio-Focused Carousel: Located in the Kiddieland area, this carousel has been billed as “a love letter to Ohio.” The carousel boasts 30 rideable characters and two chariots. The artwork represents all 88 counties with a storybook theme based on the Ohio First Lady’s literary work with Imagination Library books. The carousel does require a paid ride ticket.

    Agriculture Center: With over 100,000 square feet of space, the Agriculture Center includes the Ohio Proud Showcase and the ImAGine Exhibit. The ImAGine Exhibit is free to explore and offers a hands-on, immersive experience with crop zones, tractor simulators, drone games, and selfie stations.

    Town Square: Located just outside the entrance to Natural Resources Park, this area is perfect for taking a break! There is ample seating, a small playground, and a splash pad.

    Ohio Showcase Building: With a primary focus on its food hall (no purchase necessary), this space highlights the best of what is made in Ohio.

    If you are a window shopper, take a walk around the Bricker Marketplace or South Commercial Marketplace. Each location features specialty-made goods and engaging exhibits, including traffic safety activities from ODOT and animal displays.

    The Ohio State Fair runs from July 29–August 9, 2026.

    Address:
    717 E. 17th Ave.
    Columbus, OH 43211

    https://www.ohiostatefair.com/

      Melanie Bange
      By day, Melanie works full time in the fields of education, social service, and juvenile justice. By night, Melanie is a partner (Wes), mother to an infant (Otis), support parent to a teenager and elementary schooler (Maddie and Wesley), and suburban farmer (4 chickens) among other roles. Growing up as a Navy Brat with family from Northern Louisiana, Melanie created roots in Central Ohio based on access to travel, diversity, and Midwest honesty. Melanie prides herself on enjoying local businesses, finding low cost family opportunities, and prioritizing self-care. On a weekend, you may find Melanie at a Farmer's Market, museum, coffee shop, restaurant, trying out a new recipe, or traveling on a day trip away from Central Ohio. A typical date night for Melanie includes riding on the back of a Victory motorcycle, exploring a record shop, or attending a concert. Melanie and family love to kayak, hike, shop, explore museum exhibits, play board games (especially Sleeping Queens), paint, and dabble in "try nights" (trying a variety of junk food after eating a nutritious meal). Follow along with Melanie and the family's adventures on Instagram at ohiogirl.travelingworld
